lead: Rule 42: a boat races on wind and water alone. Part 4 adds no outside help, lifejackets under flag Y and limits on crew and gear.

sections.title: Wind and water only

qa.q: Under rule 42, what may the crew do to make the boat go faster?
qa.a: Under **rule 42.1** only the wind and the water may move the boat: you may trim to every puff, hike, bail and back a sail, but not paddle or otherwise propel her by moving your bodies.

refs: RRS Part 4 preamble, RRS definition Racing

blocks.p: You may use only the wind and the water to increase, maintain or decrease speed. The crew may **adjust the trim** of sails and hull and perform other acts of seamanship, but not otherwise move their bodies to propel the boat. Trimming to every puff, hiking, one shift of weight then held, bailing and backing a sail are legal; a paddle or a swimmer pushing the bow is not.

fig.note: A backed mainsail uses the wind; keep clear (rule 21)

blocks.p: Part 4 applies only while you are **racing**: from the preparatory signal until you have finished and cleared the line and marks. Rule 42 has no wind limit.

sections.title: Five actions that are always out

qa.q: What counts as pumping, rocking or ooching under rule 42.2?
qa.a: **Pumping** is repeated fanning of a sail, rocking repeated rolling of the boat, ooching a sudden forward body movement stopped abruptly. Rule 42.2 also bans sculling and repeated tacks or gybes unrelated to wind changes or tactics.

head: Action
What it is
rows: Pumping
Repeated fanning of a sail, by trimming and releasing or by body movement
Rocking
Repeated rolling of the boat by body movement, repeated sail or centreboard adjustment, or steering
Ooching
Sudden forward body movement, stopped abruptly
Sculling
Repeated helm movement that is forceful, propels the boat forward or stops her moving astern
Repeated tacks or gybes
Unrelated to changes in the wind or to tactics

blocks.p: The key word is **repeated**. Trimming thirty times on a shifty beat answers the wind; fanning the sail in rhythm does not. Tacking on every header is tactics; gybing every fifteen seconds down an empty run is not.

fig.note: Steady wind, nobody near: gybe after gybe is propulsion

qa.q: Can I pump the sail to catch a wave or start planing under rule 42.3?
qa.a: Yes, once: under **rule 42.3** you may pull in each sail once per wave or gust to start surfing or planing, but not upwind; when foiling, any number of times.

head: You may
Limit
rows: Roll the boat to help steer
Not repeated rolling that propels her
Roll through a tack or gybe
No faster just after it than without it
Pull each sail in once per wave or gust
To start surfing or planing, not upwind (foiling: any number)
Scull when stopped or slow above close-hauled
Only down to close-hauled
Pump to free an inverted batten
Unless it clearly propels the boat
Move the helm repeatedly
To reduce speed
Use any propulsion
To help someone in danger
Push off after grounding or collision
Either crew's force, any gear but an engine

fig.note: Stopped in the shaded sector: scull to its edge, no further

blocks.p: An exception covers only what it names: one body lunge per wave is still ooching. An engine to get off a shoal needs the sailing instructions' permission.

fig.note: Aground: crews may push by hand; no tow under engine

sections.title: Protests, yellow flags and flag O

qa.q: Can I take penalty turns for breaking rule 42, such as pumping?
qa.a: No: rule 44 turns cover only Part 2 and rule 31, so a boat that knows she broke **rule 42** retires. Only under Appendix P can a judge's first yellow flag be answered with a Two-Turns Penalty.

refs: RRS Appendix B, rule 42 as changed

blocks.p: Without judges, rule 42 is enforced by protest and a hearing. Rule 44 turns cover only Part 2 and rule 31: a boat that knows she broke rule 42 retires. **Appendix P** applies only if the notice of race or sailing instructions say so; then a judge whistles, points a yellow flag and hails your sail number.

head: Yellow flag
Penalty
rows: First
Two-Turns Penalty; if not taken, disqualified without a hearing
Second
Retire; if not, a disqualification that cannot be discarded
Third
Retire and still score DNE; if not, DNE in every race

blocks.p: A penalty cancelled by a postponement, general recall or abandonment still counts towards your total, and one incident is penalised once. Redress is possible only if the judge ignored a committee signal or a class rule. Class rules may change rule 42: where they allow pumping, rocking and ooching above a set wind, flag O switches that on and flag R switches it off. Windsurfers (Appendix B) may pump.

qa.q: Can my coach give me advice during a race, rule 41?
qa.a: No: **rule 41** forbids outside help, so a coach's tip, an arranged signal or spares handed over break it. Exceptions include help for a crew member ill, injured or in danger, information freely available to all, and unsolicited information from a disinterested source.

blocks.p: Rule 41 forbids **outside help**, with four exceptions: help for a crew member who is ill, injured or in danger; help from the other vessel's crew to get clear after a collision; information freely available to all; unsolicited information from a disinterested source, even another competitor. A coach's tip, an arranged signal, a question to a spectator, food or spares handed over all break it.

head: Rule
In short
rows: Off moorings at the preparatory signal; later made fast or hauled out only to bail, reef or repair. You may anchor or stand on the bottom; recover the anchor if you can
On board: a person in charge named by the entrant
No trash in the water on purpose, at any time afloat; coaches too
Only equipment on board at the preparatory signal. Leave the boat only when ill, injured, helping someone in danger or swimming; be back in contact before she sails on

fig.note: No wind, foul tide: you anchor, the others drift back

qa.q: When must I wear a lifejacket in a race under flag Y?
qa.a: When **flag Y** is shown with one sound: afloat before or with the warning signal, for that whole race even once lowered; ashore, all day afloat. A wetsuit or drysuit is not a lifejacket.

blocks.p: Flag Y with one sound, shown afloat before or with the warning signal, makes lifejackets compulsory for that race, even once lowered; shown ashore, all day afloat. One may come off briefly to change clothing. A wetsuit or drysuit is not a lifejacket. Without flag Y, adequate flotation is each competitor's own responsibility.

head: Rule
In short
rows: Hiking straps and thigh stiffeners only. Torso inside taut lifelines except briefly for a task; with two lifelines a seated crew may lean over the upper
No clothing to add weight; normally 8 kg at most; a quick-release trapeze harness
Ballast and unset sails stay stowed; rigging and appendages worked by hand
No polymer or textured surface to ease the water's flow; headsail tacks on the centreline
One pole in use; a headsail clew on a whisker pole (no spinnaker set) or sheeted to the main boom; a new sail may be set before the old one is lowered
Lights, fog signals and traffic separation as COLREGs require; a required tracker stays on
